summary: CROSS JOIN pairs every row in one table with every row in another. It has no matching condition.
points: The result has the row counts multiplied together, so it can get large.
It's useful for creating every possible combination, such as each student with each course.
A LEFT JOIN from that grid then fills in what happened, leaving 0 where nothing did.
An accidental missing ON has the same effect, which is usually a bug.

example.sql:
SELECT s.name, c.title, COUNT(e.id) AS attempts
FROM students s
CROSS JOIN courses c
LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id AND e.course_id = c.id
GROUP BY s.id, s.name, c.id, c.title;
example.explanation: Every student and course pair appears, including pairs with zero attempts.
